name: customer-support
description: Customer support and sales fundamentals: communication skills, CRM tools, sales techniques, conflict resolution, product knowledge, and support workflows. Built on top of high-school-graduate base.

facts.fact: Active listening means fully focusing on the speaker, understanding their message, and responding thoughtfully rather than just waiting to speak
facts.query: active listening focus understand respond

facts.fact: Empathy in customer service means understanding and acknowledging the customer's feelings and perspective without necessarily agreeing with them
facts.query: empathy customer feelings perspective acknowledge

facts.fact: Positive language focuses on what can be done rather than what cannot, such as saying Let me find that for you instead of I don't know
facts.query: positive language can do cannot customer

facts.fact: Open-ended questions encourage detailed responses and start with what, how, why, or tell me about, while closed questions get yes/no answers
facts.query: open-ended questions detailed responses what how why

facts.fact: Paraphrasing means restating the customer's concern in your own words to confirm understanding before addressing it
facts.query: paraphrasing restate confirm understanding concern

facts.fact: Tone of voice in written communication is conveyed through word choice, punctuation, and formatting, since the reader cannot hear your voice
facts.query: tone of voice written communication word choice

facts.fact: De-escalation techniques include staying calm, using a low steady voice, acknowledging the person's frustration, and focusing on solutions
facts.query: de-escalation calm steady voice acknowledge frustration

facts.fact: The LAER model (Listen, Acknowledge, Explore, Respond) is a framework for handling customer objections and concerns
facts.query: LAER listen acknowledge explore respond objections

facts.fact: Professional communication in customer support means being courteous, clear, concise, and free of jargon the customer may not understand
facts.query: professional communication courteous clear concise jargon

facts.fact: A follow-up after resolving an issue shows the customer you care about their satisfaction and helps prevent future problems
facts.query: follow-up after resolve satisfaction prevent

facts.fact: A CRM (Customer Relationship Management) system tracks all customer interactions, data, and history in one place, with popular platforms including Salesforce, HubSpot, and Zendesk
facts.query: CRM customer relationship management Salesforce HubSpot Zendesk

facts.fact: A ticketing system organizes customer support requests into trackable tickets with status, priority, and assignment
facts.query: ticketing system support requests priority assignment

facts.fact: First contact resolution (FCR) measures the percentage of issues resolved on the first interaction without escalation or follow-up
facts.query: first contact resolution FCR percentage first interaction

facts.fact: An SLA (Service Level Agreement) defines the expected response and resolution times that support commits to for different priority levels
facts.query: SLA service level agreement response resolution time

facts.fact: A knowledge base is a searchable library of articles, FAQs, and guides that customers and agents use to find answers
facts.query: knowledge base articles FAQs guides searchable

facts.fact: An omnichannel support approach provides consistent service across all channels: email, phone, chat, social media, and self-service
facts.query: omnichannel support consistent email phone chat social

facts.fact: Customer satisfaction score (CSAT) measures how happy customers are with a support interaction, typically via a post-interaction survey
facts.query: CSAT customer satisfaction score survey

facts.fact: Net Promoter Score (NPS) asks customers how likely they are to recommend the company on a scale of 0-10 and categorizes them as promoters, passives, or detractors
facts.query: NPS net promoter score recommend 0-10

facts.fact: Average handle time (AHT) measures the average duration of a customer interaction from start to finish
facts.query: average handle time AHT duration interaction

facts.fact: A chatbot can handle common, repetitive questions automatically, freeing human agents for complex issues
facts.query: chatbot common questions automatic human agents

facts.fact: The sales funnel has stages: prospecting (finding leads), qualifying (assessing fit), presenting (showing value), handling objections, closing (getting commitment), and follow-up
facts.query: sales funnel prospecting qualifying presenting closing

facts.fact: SPIN selling uses Situation, Problem, Implication, and Need-payoff questions to guide the customer toward recognizing their need
facts.query: SPIN selling situation problem implication need payoff

facts.fact: An upsell encourages the customer to buy a higher-end version of the product, while a cross-sell suggests complementary products
facts.query: upsell cross-sell higher end complementary

facts.fact: Value-based selling focuses on the benefits and outcomes the customer will experience, not just the features of the product
facts.query: value-based selling benefits outcomes not features

facts.fact: Handling objections involves listening to the concern, validating it, and providing a specific response that addresses the root worry
facts.query: handling objections listening validating response concern

facts.fact: A qualified lead is a prospect who has the budget, authority, need, and timeline (BANT) to make a purchase decision
facts.query: qualified lead BANT budget authority need timeline

facts.fact: Consultative selling positions the salesperson as a trusted advisor who diagnoses the customer's needs before recommending a solution
facts.query: consultative selling trusted advisor diagnose needs

facts.fact: A closing technique is a method for getting the customer to commit, such as the assumptive close (When would you like delivery?) or the summary close (recapping benefits)
facts.query: closing technique commit assumptive summary

facts.fact: Building rapport means establishing a genuine connection with the customer through shared interests, friendly conversation, and authentic interest
facts.query: building rapport connection shared interests friendly

facts.fact: The lifetime value of a customer (LTV) is the total revenue a customer is expected to generate over their entire relationship with the company
facts.query: lifetime value LTV customer revenue relationship

facts.fact: The HEARD model for difficult interactions is: Hear, Empathize, Apologize, Resolve, and Diagnose to prevent recurrence
facts.query: HEARD hear empathize apologize resolve diagnose

facts.fact: When a customer is angry, the first step is to let them vent completely before attempting to solve the problem
facts.query: angry customer vent first step before solving

facts.fact: Acknowledging the customer's frustration without placing blame validates their feelings and reduces tension
facts.query: acknowledge frustration validate feelings tension

facts.fact: Taking ownership of a problem means accepting responsibility to fix it, even if you did not cause it
facts.query: ownership responsibility fix not caused

facts.fact: Escalation to a supervisor should be offered when the customer requests it, when policy limits are reached, or when the issue is beyond the agent's authority
facts.query: escalation supervisor policy limits authority

facts.fact: Compromise means finding a middle ground where both the company and customer give up something to reach agreement
facts.query: compromise middle ground agreement company customer

facts.fact: Setting clear expectations about timelines and next steps prevents frustration caused by uncertainty
facts.query: setting expectations timelines next steps uncertainty

facts.fact: Following company policies while remaining flexible enough to find creative solutions within those policies is key to effective resolution
facts.query: company policies flexible creative solutions

facts.fact: Deep product knowledge enables support agents to answer questions confidently, identify the root cause of issues, and suggest relevant features
facts.query: product knowledge root cause features confident

facts.fact: Reproducing a customer's issue means following the same steps they took to confirm the problem before attempting a fix
facts.query: reproducing issue same steps confirm fix

facts.fact: A workaround is a temporary solution that allows the customer to proceed while a permanent fix is being developed
facts.query: workaround temporary solution permanent fix

facts.fact: Tiered support has levels: Tier 1 handles common questions, Tier 2 handles complex issues, and Tier 3 handles advanced or engineering-level problems
facts.query: tiered support Tier 1 2 3 common complex engineering

facts.fact: Root cause analysis identifies the underlying reason for an issue rather than just treating the symptoms
facts.query: root cause analysis underlying reason symptoms

facts.fact: Bug reports should include steps to reproduce, expected behavior, actual behavior, environment, and screenshots
facts.query: bug report steps reproduce expected actual environment

facts.fact: Onboarding new customers includes guiding them through setup, explaining key features, and setting expectations for the product experience
facts.query: onboarding setup features expectations new customer

facts.fact: Customer feedback collected through surveys, reviews, and direct conversations should be shared with product teams to drive improvements
facts.query: customer feedback surveys reviews product improvements

facts.fact: Self-service resources like FAQs, video tutorials, and community forums reduce support volume by helping customers solve problems independently
facts.query: self-service FAQs tutorials forums reduce volume

facts.fact: A support workflow defines the steps from ticket creation through triage, assignment, investigation, resolution, and closure
facts.query: support workflow triage assignment investigation resolution
